lines.japanese: おはようございます。
lines.english: Good morning.

lines.japanese: ふぁ……ーぁふ。
lines.english: Yaaawn.

lines.japanese: まどろみから目覚めてみると、俺の体は、ところどころ空席の残る午後の電車に揺られていました。
lines.english: When I surfaced from my doze, I found myself being rocked by an afternoon train with empty seats scattered throughout.

lines.japanese: よく見知った景色が窓の外をゆったり流れています──残念ながら、望む方向とは反対に。
lines.english: A deeply familiar landscape drifted past the windows—regrettably, in the opposite direction from the one I desired.

lines.japanese: ええ、つまり、やれやれです。
lines.english: Yes. In other words: here we go again.

lines.japanese: 「次はー、かざみがおかー、風見ヶ丘です。急行電車の待ち合わせが……」
lines.english: “Next stop, Kazamigaoka—Kazamigaoka. Passengers transferring to the express...”

lines.japanese: ふぅ。
lines.english: Sigh.

lines.japanese: 俺はロングシートから腰を上げて、ドアの前へ移動しておきました。次の駅で降りて、上り電車に乗りなおさなくてはならないからです。
lines.english: I rose from the bench and moved to the doors. I would have to get off at the next station and catch a train back the other way.

lines.japanese: ま、こんなことは、慢性的な睡眠不足に悩まされているこの身にはよくあることでして、ことさら慌てふためくほどのことでも──
lines.english: For a man plagued by chronic sleep deprivation, this sort of thing was commonplace. It hardly merited—

lines.japanese: ──あ、そうだ。せっかく出来た手持ち無沙汰な時間を、ただ無為に浪費するなんてもったいない。
lines.english: —ah, of course. What a waste it would be to let this unexpected spell of idleness pass unused.

lines.japanese: 俺は流れる風見ヶ丘の街並に寄りかかって荷物を開きました。
lines.english: With Kazamigaoka sliding past outside, I opened my bag.

lines.japanese: 取りだしたのは一冊の文庫本。
lines.english: Out came a single paperback.

lines.japanese: 細川玉木著、『ほほえみインサイド』。
lines.english: *Smile Inside*, by Tamaki Hosokawa.

lines.japanese: 「やなぎはらー、やなぎはらー」
lines.english: “Yanagihara—Yanagihara.”

lines.japanese: 「終点ー、柳木原です。お忘れ物ないようご注意ください」
lines.english: “This is the final stop, Yanagihara. Please take care not to leave any belongings behind.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　あっ？　おわっ、終点か！」
lines.english: “What? Ah! Whoa—the final stop!”

lines.japanese: 俺は開いていたページにしおりを挿んで、慌ててホームへ飛びだしました──
lines.english: I shoved a bookmark between the open pages and rushed onto the platform—

lines.japanese: ──と、まあ、周囲が見えなくなるぐらい、物語に熱中していたのです。
lines.english: —which should convey how utterly the story had consumed me, to the exclusion of the world around me.

lines.japanese: だって、ええ、バイト仲間のひいき目抜きに、ほんとほんと、素で面白いと思いますよこれ。ほほえみインサイド。
lines.english: And yes, setting aside all favoritism toward a coworker, I truly, honestly found it delightful. *Smile Inside*, that is.

lines.japanese: 主人公は曲がったことが大嫌いな女の子。お相手はちょっと不良だけどホントは優しい男の子。そんなふたりが微笑ましい衝突を重ねながらも、甘酸っぱい気持ちを育んでゆく純愛物語。
lines.english: Its heroine was a girl who despised anything crooked or unjust. Her counterpart was a boy who acted like a delinquent but had a gentle heart. Through one charming collision after another, the two nurtured the tender, bittersweet stirrings of pure young love.

lines.japanese: 懐かしささえ覚えるステロタイプな王道ラブコメですが、ま、王道は王道ゆえに王道ってなもんで、読んでる側の期待どおりに嵌ってゆく展開が、実に心地よいと言うか胸おどると言うか。
lines.english: It was a classic romantic comedy, so conventional as to feel nostalgic. But a classic becomes a classic for good reason, and there was something deeply satisfying—something exhilarating—about watching every development click precisely into the shape a reader hoped for.

lines.japanese: 作者の日和子さん自身も実はこんな乙女ちっくなロマンスに憧れているのかしら、なんてつい勘繰ってしまうのは、読み方としちゃ間違ってるんでしょうけど。
lines.english: Perhaps Hiyoko herself secretly dreamed of this same girlish romance. It was probably wrong to read an author that way, but I couldn't help wondering.

lines.japanese: それは抜きにしても、ええ、面白いです。まあ「面白い」にもいろいろありますけど、たとえば読んでてあったかい気持ちになってしまう、あの良質な少女漫画の雰囲気なんです。
lines.english: Even leaving that aside, yes, it was delightful. It had the warmth of a first-rate girls' romance comic, the kind that left a glow inside you as you read.

lines.japanese: シンプルだけど決して稚拙さは感じさせない筆致に、ときおり作者ならではの繊細なセンスが垣間見えるあたり、読みやすくて心に沁みるバランスのいい文章だなあ、なんて偉そうに思ってしまう千歳鷲介でした。
lines.english: The prose was simple without ever feeling childish, and now and then it revealed flashes of the author's uniquely delicate sensibility. Accessible yet affecting, perfectly balanced—or so Shusuke Chitose presumptuously concluded.

lines.japanese: 「というわけで、米田さんもその本読んだ方がいいっすよ」
lines.english: “Which is why you ought to read it too, Yoneda.”

lines.japanese: 「え、なんすかその、ノーリアクション」
lines.english: “What's with the complete lack of reaction?”

lines.japanese: 「千歳君ってさ、ここ来るたび、必ずなにか私に薦めていくよね」
lines.english: “Every time you come here, Chitose, you end up recommending something to me.”

lines.japanese: 米田さんは無関心な調子で言いながら、俺に差しだしていた細川玉木の著作二点を机の上に戻しました。
lines.english: Yoneda spoke with supreme indifference as she returned the two Tamaki Hosokawa books to the desk.

lines.japanese: 「もったいない。タダであげようと思ってたのに、自腹切って買っちゃったんだ？」
lines.english: “What a waste. I was going to give them to you for free, but you went and bought them with your own money?”

lines.japanese: 「え、ちょっとアナタ、その本出してる会社の社員でしょう。そこは毎度ありと言ってくださいよ」
lines.english: “Hold on. You work for the company that publishes those books. This is where you're supposed to thank me for my business.”

lines.japanese: 「べーっつに、文庫がいくら売れたって、私のお昼のＡ定がＳ定になるわけでもなし？　んーなん知ったこっちゃねーですよ」
lines.english: “As if I care. Selling another paperback isn't going to upgrade my lunch from the basic set to the deluxe one. I couldn't care less.”

lines.japanese: 「愛社精神うすっ」
lines.english: “Your company loyalty is paper-thin.”

lines.japanese: 「恒産なくして恒心なしって言うでしょ。私、大らかな気持ちを養えるほど大らかなお金もらってないもん」
lines.english: “You know what they say: no steady income, no steady heart. They don't pay me generously enough to make me feel generous.”

lines.japanese: 「言いますね」
lines.english: “Very eloquent.”

lines.japanese: 「言わせてよ、この目のクマが取れないうちは」
lines.english: “Let me have my say. At least until these dark circles disappear.”

lines.japanese: 「あら、今日も今日とて睡眠不足ですか」
lines.english: “My, my. Short on sleep again today?”

lines.japanese: 「好きで選んだ仕事だから仕方ないんだけどさ、それはそれとして愚痴のひとつやふたつはこぼしたいよね」
lines.english: “I chose this work because I love it, so that part can't be helped. But I'd still like the right to complain once or twice.”

lines.japanese: 「そういうものですか？」
lines.english: “Is that how it works?”

lines.japanese: 「だーって、学生時代に築きあげてきたかけがえのない友情が、ひとつまたひとつと失われていくのとかさー？　えー、どうなのよ、それは。はぁ、やるせないわ～」
lines.english: “I mean, watching the irreplaceable friendships you built in school vanish one after another? What are you supposed to make of that? Ugh. It's tragic.”

lines.japanese: 入社以来どれだけの数、飲みや遊びの誘いを断ってきたことか。そうぼやいて、米田さんはしくしくと泣きくずれる真似をしました。
lines.english: How many invitations for drinks and outings had she turned down since joining the company? Yoneda lamented the number, then pretended to collapse in tears.

lines.japanese: オトナって大変だなあ。
lines.english: Being an adult looked hard.

lines.japanese: 「で、原稿は？」
lines.english: “So. The manuscript?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、はいはい」
lines.english: “Oh, yes, of course.”

lines.japanese: しゃっきりと気を取りなおした働くおねえさんに、俺は文字で埋めてきた原稿用紙を提出しました。
lines.english: Now all business again, she sat waiting as I handed over the manuscript pages I had filled.

lines.japanese: 「これが多摩いづみの紹介文ね？　はーい、玉稿いただきましたー」
lines.english: “This is the profile of Tama Izumi, right? Very good—your illustrious manuscript is received.”

lines.japanese: そしてそれは、今日もほとんど目を通されることなく封筒の中へ運ばれていきました。
lines.english: And today as well, it traveled into an envelope with hardly a glance cast over it.

lines.japanese: 「そいで？　細川玉木レビューの方はど？」
lines.english: “And how's the Tamaki Hosokawa review coming?”

lines.japanese: 「はい、ぼちぼち。たぶん来週ぐらいには」
lines.english: “Bit by bit. I'll probably have it next week.”

lines.japanese: 「そ？　じゃあ、頑張って」
lines.english: “Will you? Then keep at it.”

lines.japanese: と微笑んでから、ふと思いだしたように彼女がさっきの二冊を拾いあげました。
lines.english: She smiled, then seemed to remember something and picked up the two books again.

lines.japanese: 「ところで、どっちの紹介文書いてるんだっけ？」
lines.english: “By the way, which one are you reviewing?”

lines.japanese: 年齢より若く見える米田さんの童顔を挟んで、対照的なふたつの表紙が並んでいます。『ほほえみインサイド』と『米寿』。
lines.english: The two contrasting covers stood on either side of Yoneda's face, which looked younger than her years: *Smile Inside* and *Eighty-Eight*.

lines.japanese: 「はあ。どっちがいんすか」
lines.english: “Well? Which one should I do?”

lines.japanese: 「んっ？」
lines.english: “Hm?”

lines.japanese: 彼女は評価不調の『米寿』を下ろして、人気作の方を少々前へ突きだしてきました。
lines.english: She lowered the poorly received *Eighty-Eight* and pushed the popular book slightly forward.

lines.japanese: 「きのう下の階の同期に聞いたんだけど、こっち、いまだにちょろちょろ出てるらしいよ」
lines.english: “I asked a colleague downstairs yesterday. Apparently this one is still selling a few copies here and there.”

lines.japanese: 「え、そっちは？」
lines.english: “What about the other one?”

lines.japanese: 俺は米田さんの膝の上へ伏せられてしまった方に目を寄せました。彼女は「ああ」と言いながら、二冊を机の隅に押しもどしました。
lines.english: I looked toward the book she had laid facedown across her lap. ‘Oh, that,’ she said, pushing both volumes back into one corner of the desk.

lines.japanese: 「一作目の評判が良かったから、初版だけはわりと出たらしいけど。それっきり伸びなかったって」
lines.english: “The first book had a good reputation, so apparently the initial print run sold fairly well. But that was as far as it went.”

lines.japanese: 「あら、おかしいですね。不思議な現象もあったものです」
lines.english: “How odd. What a mysterious phenomenon.”

lines.japanese: 「不思議もなにも。単純に受けなかっただけでしょ」
lines.english: “There's no mystery. People simply didn't like it.”

lines.japanese: 「うわ、言っちゃったよこのひと！」
lines.english: “Good heavens, she came right out and said it!”

lines.japanese: 「うち版元だもん、言う権利あるでしょ？」
lines.english: “We're the publisher. That gives me the right, doesn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「愛社精神ないくせにー」
lines.english: “Despite your total lack of company loyalty?”

lines.japanese: 「ないとは言ってないの。わりと薄いだけ」
lines.english: “I never said it was totally absent. It's merely rather thin.”

lines.japanese: 「え、それでは、祥玄社さんとしては細川玉木という作家について現在どのようにお考えで？」
lines.english: “Then what is Shogensha's current opinion of Tamaki Hosokawa as an author?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、その同期の子が言うにはだけど、編集部は完全に後悔ムード漂ってるみたい。一発目は単にフロックだったんだろって」
lines.english: “Well, this is according to my colleague, but apparently the editorial department is steeped in regret. They've decided the first book was a fluke.”

lines.japanese: 「つまり、まぐれ当たりってことすか？」
lines.english: “In other words, a lucky hit?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。若くしてデビューしちゃった子って、そういうのよくあるんだって。資質を見抜けないで選んじゃった方にも問題あるんだろうけど」
lines.english: “Right. She says that happens a lot with writers who debut young. Though I suppose some blame lies with the people who selected them without recognizing whether they had real talent.”

lines.japanese: 「あとほら、若いってことは発展途上ってことだから。成長が早い分、すぐ自分の過去作に嫌気がさしたりして、なかなか筆が安定しないんだって」
lines.english: “And being young means you're still developing. The faster you grow, the sooner you may start hating your earlier work, so your writing never has a chance to settle into anything consistent.”

lines.japanese: ああ……。
lines.english: Ah...

lines.japanese: そういや英里子さんが言ってたな、二作目は作風を変えようと力んでるのが感じられたって。
lines.english: Eriko had said something similar: she could feel the second book straining to change its style.

lines.japanese: 「それで、もしその若き雛鳥がより良いものを生みだそうと必死にもがいて、でも結果、お客さんや編集の望まないものが誕生しちゃったとしたら、それは不幸だよね」
lines.english: “So suppose that young fledgling struggled desperately to create something better, but the result was something neither her readers nor her editors wanted. That would be a tragedy, wouldn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「不幸、ですか？」
lines.english: “A tragedy, you say?”

lines.japanese: 「そ、不幸。書いたひとも書かせたひとも、買ったひとも読んだひとも、刷ったひとも並べたひともみんなが不幸」
lines.english: “Exactly. A tragedy. The person who wrote it, the person who commissioned it, the people who bought it and read it, the people who printed it and put it on the shelves—everyone ends up miserable.”

lines.japanese: ……せつない話です。
lines.english: ...A painful story.

lines.japanese: 日和子さんに初めて会った日、彼女が泣きだしそうな笑顔で俺に投げかけてきた言葉を思いだしました。
lines.english: I remembered the words Hiyoko had offered me on the day we first met, smiling as though she might burst into tears.

lines.japanese: 『どんな形であれ……』
lines.english: “Whatever form it takes...”

lines.japanese: 『書いたものを読んでもらえるっていうのは、やっぱり、嬉しいんです』
lines.english: “Having someone read what you wrote still makes you happy.”

lines.japanese: ほんと、せつない話。
lines.english: A painful story indeed.

lines.japanese: 俺は明るい声で米田さんに尋ねました。
lines.english: In a bright voice, I asked Yoneda a question.
